coverage_review.method: Fresh agent read only the raw article and extracted 268 clause-level spans before seeing this replacement ledger; the spans were then grouped into atomic material claims and compared row-by-row

claims.quote: the perception of the body is the perception of the land
claims.evidence_rationale: The author explicitly locates this as a recurring thought arising during reflection; the article treats it as a situated thesis, not a universal measurement.

claims.quote: each division can also teach the mind what kind of world it inhabits
claims.transformation: The essay maps repeated bodily and territorial classification onto habits of attention without claiming a measured universal effect.
claims.evidence_rationale: Internal Noesis authorship is explicit here; the public article presents the relation as the author’s inquiry.

claims.quote: The Bhagavad Gītā names the body as kṣetra, the field, and distinguishes it from the knower of the field, kṣetrajña
claims.evidence_rationale: The source is named and linked; the article does not treat the verse as biological evidence.

claims.quote: Eigenwelt, the world of one’s own lived interior; Umwelt, the surrounding world as encountered through a body; and Mitwelt, the shared world
claims.evidence_rationale: The linked reference attributes the three worlds to Ludwig Binswanger and gives the surrounding/shared/self-world distinctions used here.

claims.quote: one names the body as a field to be known, while the other distinguishes the worlds that meet within knowing
claims.transformation: Comparison of two non-equivalent vocabularies by the relational work they perform.
claims.evidence_rationale: Noesis authorship is internal; public prose explicitly says the terms do different work rather than presenting equivalence.

claims.quote: The Puruṣa Sūkta gives an image of cosmic order through a primordial person whose parts correspond to a larger social and cosmic arrangement
claims.evidence_rationale: The hymn is named and linked; its primordial-person and part-to-order imagery is reported as traditional material.

claims.quote: The Bhūmi Sūkta addresses Earth as ground, mother, and bearer of many peoples
claims.evidence_rationale: The hymn is named and linked; mother, earth, and plural-peoples language occur within the hymn.

claims.quote: In these hymns, body and ground become parallel instruments for thinking about order, plurality, obligation, and belonging
claims.transformation: The essay compares two linked hymn images while expressly denying that either is a modern blueprint.
claims.evidence_rationale: The conclusion stays at the level of interpretive use and does not infer anatomy, statecraft, or causation from the hymns.
claims.public_boundary: Cross-text interpretation with explicit historical boundary

claims.quote: every map begins from an embodied coordinate
claims.transformation: The thesis condenses field, world, body, and ground into the claim that mapping is first encountered from embodiment.
claims.evidence_rationale: This is the essay’s central Noesis-authored interpretation and is presented publicly as a way of noticing.

claims.quote: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa treats the cycles as recurring rather than as a one-time ladder of progress
claims.evidence_rationale: The named chapter is linked and the article keeps its yuga material in cosmological rather than modern historical time.

claims.quote: Read as a diagnostic rather than a stopwatch, the yugas describe four conditions of relation
claims.transformation: Cosmological time is converted into an explicitly modern relational diagnostic without being attributed back to the source.
claims.evidence_rationale: Internal Noesis authorship is explicit; public prose marks the move with ‘Read as’ and denies dateable-history equivalence.

claims.quote: Satya names a condition in which relation is comparatively transparent
claims.transformation: Satya is interpreted through legible boundary and relational transparency.
claims.evidence_rationale: The section’s preceding sentence marks all four conditions as a modern diagnostic.

claims.quote: Tretā introduces measure, vow, and institution
claims.transformation: Tretā is interpreted as structure that permits transmission and can harden into hierarchy.
claims.evidence_rationale: The claim remains inside the declared diagnostic reading.

claims.quote: Dvāpara is the condition of competing obligations
claims.transformation: Dvāpara is interpreted through contextual discernment under conflicting duties.
claims.evidence_rationale: The claim remains inside the declared diagnostic reading and makes no chronology claim.

claims.quote: Kali names a condition of contraction, noise, and weakened relation
claims.transformation: Kali is interpreted as signs and institutions persisting after losing contact with living purpose.
claims.evidence_rationale: The claim remains inside the declared diagnostic reading.

claims.quote: The same person can inhabit all four in one day
claims.transformation: The cosmological sequence is rescaled into coexisting relational conditions rather than a ranking of people.
claims.evidence_rationale: This is interpretive and not presented as a measured psychological frequency.

claims.quote: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa gives a longer sequence and then says that incarnations are innumerable
claims.evidence_rationale: The linked chapter enumerates more than ten avatāras and states that incarnations are innumerable.

claims.quote: Jayadeva’s Gīta Govinda presents a tenfold poetic arrangement
claims.evidence_rationale: The linked text presents the tenfold poetic sequence; the article no longer makes an unsupported popularity or reception-history claim.

claims.quote: The list is therefore a pedagogical constellation, not a single universally fixed table
claims.transformation: Variant enumerations are used to reject a single universally fixed ten-item table.
claims.evidence_rationale: The inference is no stronger than the two differently sized source arrangements.

claims.quote: The sequence becomes more useful when read as a series of forms answering conditions
claims.transformation: The listed forms are compared by the kind of damaged field or constraint to which each story responds.
claims.evidence_rationale: Internal Noesis authorship is explicit; public prose later says this is a modern reading, not Purāṇic vocabulary.

claims.quote: Matsya preserves what would otherwise be lost: continuity under flood
claims.transformation: The fish/flood narrative is abstracted as continuity under destructive conditions.
claims.evidence_rationale: One atomic member of the declared modern avatar reading.

claims.quote: Kūrma supports a collective undertaking: patience made load-bearing
claims.transformation: The tortoise support narrative is abstracted as load-bearing patience.
claims.evidence_rationale: One atomic member of the declared modern avatar reading.

claims.quote: Varāha retrieves ground from submersion: a world re-grounded
claims.transformation: The boar/earth narrative is abstracted as re-grounding.
claims.evidence_rationale: One atomic member of the declared modern avatar reading.

claims.quote: Narasiṃha breaks a binary that has become legally airtight
claims.transformation: The man-lion and boon-boundary narrative is abstracted as exceeding an airtight category without abolishing order.
claims.evidence_rationale: One atomic member of the declared modern avatar reading.

claims.quote: Vāmana changes scale, measuring possession against the space life actually occupies
claims.transformation: The dwarf/three-strides narrative is abstracted as a change of scale that tests possession.
claims.evidence_rationale: One atomic member of the declared modern avatar reading.

claims.quote: Paraśurāma interrupts force that has mistaken inheritance for entitlement
claims.transformation: The warrior narrative is abstracted as interruption of corrupted inherited authority.
claims.evidence_rationale: One atomic member of the declared modern avatar reading.

claims.quote: Rāma gives form to maryādā, the discipline of a boundary and a vow
claims.transformation: Rāma is read through vowed boundary and disciplined limit.
claims.evidence_rationale: One atomic member of the declared modern avatar reading.

claims.quote: Kṛṣṇa acts within collision, bringing contextual intelligence to conflicting duties
claims.transformation: Kṛṣṇa is read through contextual action under conflicting obligations.
claims.evidence_rationale: One atomic member of the declared modern avatar reading.

claims.quote: Buddha, in later lists, turns toward compassion, non-harm, and release from compulsive grasping
claims.transformation: Jayadeva’s Buddha stanza is read through compassion and non-harm, with ‘later lists’ preserving the list boundary.
claims.evidence_rationale: One atomic member of the declared modern avatar reading, scoped to lists that include Buddha.

claims.quote: Kalki belongs to a future horizon in the cycle: renewal after a form has exhausted its capacity to hold relation
claims.transformation: The future avatāra is abstracted as renewal after exhausted form.
claims.evidence_rationale: One atomic member of the declared modern avatar reading.

claims.quote: Freedom is the ability to recognize which form a situation requires, and when that form has become an obstacle
claims.transformation: The ten readings are generalized into a revisable relationship between freedom and form.
claims.evidence_rationale: A philosophical conclusion presented as the essay’s implication, not as inherited doctrine.

claims.quote: the division of land can produce a divided understanding of mind
claims.transformation: The article maps repeated territorial partitions onto memory, law, language, bodily expectation, and attention.
claims.evidence_rationale: The public text calls this the author’s central proposition, uses ‘can,’ and explicitly denies mechanical psychological causation.
claims.public_boundary: Scoped interpretive proposition, not empirical causation

claims.quote: Cell is a precise biological term, a social unit, a room of confinement, and a carrier of electrical charge in a device
claims.evidence_rationale: The article explicitly states that the shared word does not make the structures the same and draws no literal mechanism across them.

claims.quote: Its membrane is selectively permeable. It maintains difference while permitting exchange
claims.evidence_rationale: The linked biology text describes selective permeability and transport through diffusion, channels, carriers, and pumps.
claims.public_boundary: Ordinary biological claim with adjacent source

claims.quote: Their ethical difference lies in who sets the boundary, what may cross it, and whether the boundary can be revised
claims.transformation: Shared boundedness is retained while agency, permeability, and revisability distinguish biological, social, prison, and contemplative cases.
claims.evidence_rationale: The comparison preserves categorical differences and makes an ethical rather than biological inference.

claims.quote: A partition imposed on land can therefore become an Umwelt condition, an Eigenwelt expectation, and a Mitwelt rule
claims.transformation: A territorial partition is mapped onto surrounding, self, and shared worlds through language, law, architecture, work, family, and memory.
claims.evidence_rationale: The statement is explicitly a cross-scale interpretation using ‘can,’ not a universal empirical law.

claims.quote: Some limits are constitutive... inherited... chosen... imposed... emergent... revisable
claims.evidence_rationale: The six-part taxonomy is an internally coherent Noesis editorial model used to prevent coercion, agency, and suffering from being collapsed.

claims.quote: Even when a person later names growth, that growth never proves the suffering was deserved or secretly selected
claims.evidence_rationale: This is a normative safety boundary within the essay’s model: possible later growth is not treated as evidence of deserved or chosen suffering.

claims.quote: Kha–Ba–La gives this discernment three terms
claims.evidence_rationale: The internal ledger identifies Kha-Ba-La as Noesis house vocabulary; the public article defines all three terms and does not attribute them to Sanskrit or Purāṇic sources.
claims.public_boundary: Defined house framework without inherited-source claim

claims.quote: Does this boundary preserve relation, or has it replaced relation?
claims.transformation: Biological permeability, ethical boundary-setting, limit taxonomy, and Kha-Ba-La are condensed into one revisability question.
claims.evidence_rationale: The public prose presents the question as portable on its own and keeps membrane and partition cases distinct.

claims.quote: Distinction is a tool; severance is the error
claims.transformation: The article’s field, yuga, avatar, partition, phenomenology, and boundary arguments are compressed into a final distinction between useful differentiation and relational severance.
claims.evidence_rationale: This is the final Noesis-authored synthesis; the article states it aphoristically without attributing it to any source.

claims.quote: The materials gathered here come from the Bhagavad Gītā, Vedic hymns, and Purāṇic texts; they do not speak from one text or in one voice
claims.transformation: The named source families used in the essay are kept distinct rather than presented as one uniform inherited system.
claims.evidence_rationale: This is an editorial source boundary derived from the separately named and linked materials, not a chronology or textual-dating claim.

claims.quote: the map begins to feel more real than the ground ... the body becomes an inventory ... the divided mind begins to experience itself as a collection of departments
claims.evidence_rationale: The sequence is framed as the essay’s motivating image and possibility, not as a measured universal causal law.
claims.public_boundary: Opening metaphor and scoped interpretive possibility

claims.quote: A field is neither a fantasy nor a pile of parts. It is a relation with conditions
claims.evidence_rationale: This is the essay’s working definition of field, introduced as authorial synthesis rather than attributed to the Gītā, phenomenology, or biology.

claims.quote: Self-Consciousness as Technology. Body as Medium. Breath as Interface
claims.evidence_rationale: The signature is recognizable Tryambakam house language. It is retained as a brand-level conceptual triad, not presented as empirical fact or inherited teaching.
